em2: Say your language — a free interpreter comes on the line.
h1: Tell us what happened — in your own words.
sub: Type or speak in your language. We help you understand your options. You decide what happens next.
tr: Free and independent — not the police, not government.
try: Try it — tap the microphone or a story below
ph: I’m not sure what to call it…
tag: Information only · AI can make mistakes
resp: This could be a workplace issue. Options people use: talk to a free community legal centre, or make a complaint at work. You decide what happens.
p1: My boss jokes about my accent at work.
p2: Children at school laugh at my daughter’s lunch.
p3: Someone online sends me threatening messages.
p5: I don’t know what to call it — I just want to talk.
howMeta: Free · about 3 minutes · works on any phone
sh: Tap the one closest to your situation.
s1d: Speak or type in your own language. Share only what you want — no names or details you don't want to give.
s1r: Your words stay on your phone until you choose to send them.
s2d: Simple information about what you can do, with links to the services behind each option.
s2r: Every answer shows where the information comes from.
s3d: Get support, make a report, or save it for later. Nothing is sent without you.
s3r: You can stop or delete at any time.
exB1: “Someone at work keeps making jokes about my accent.” — spoken or typed, in any of our 4 languages.
exB2: “You could talk to a free community legal centre, or make a complaint at work.” Each option links to its source.
exT3: 3. You choose what leaves your phone
exB3: A toggle asks before anything is sent: “Send this report?” It stays off until you turn it on.
howClose: Once you send a report, the authority takes over — SafeSpeak stays out of it.
bridgeH: Sometimes the next step is a person.
bridgeP: Talk with people who understand — free helplines, community advocates, and legal help, in your language.
sUrgentP: If you or someone else is in immediate danger, call emergency services now.
sInterp: Say your language — all these services have free interpreters.
dResp: Domestic, family and sexual violence support.
dYarn: Culturally safe crisis support for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples.
q1p: You can get information before deciding. Understanding options does not mean you have to report.
q2p: Different pathways exist depending on where you go. SafeSpeak explains possible next steps in plain language.
q3p: Messages. Photos. Dates. Documents. Keep what feels useful — only if it is safe for you to do so.
q4p: Privacy options vary by organisation. Learn what anonymity can look like before you choose a path.
dAid: Free legal information and advice across New South Wales.
dClc: Local legal support services in every state and territory.
sLegalNote: Information is general and does not replace professional legal advice.
sPrivH: Protect your privacy while seeking help.
sPrivP: Simple steps if you share a device or worry someone might see what you've looked at.
pv1p: If someone else uses this device, use a private browser window and clear recent history when it is safe.
pv2p: Visiting support sites can leave traces. Clear history when it is safe.
pv3p: Calls, messages, or app alerts can show you sought help. Silence or redirect them if needed.
pv4p: SafeSpeak needs no account. Avoid saving passwords where others can see them.
pv5p: Keep copies of messages or photos only if it is safe. Store them somewhere private.
sQuizP: Answer a few simple questions and we'll show possible options.
sQuizNote: This guided tool is part of the full SafeSpeak build.
cap: Photography of community members telling their own stories. Images are illustrative portraits, not of real clients.

r2: Your words stay on your phone until you choose to send them.
